intents.text: Add an opt-in `reverse_proxy` setting `stream_detached` (Caddyfile and JSON) that detaches upgraded streams from the config lifecycle so they survive a reload, closing on reload only streams whose upstream was removed from the new config.
Keep the default (stream_detached off) as today: upgraded streams are closed on reload, honouring the existing close-delay behaviour.
Add a `stream_logs` block (Caddyfile and JSON) with a `skip_handshake` option that suppresses access logging of the upgrade handshake (default: logged).
Emit stream close logs that are available in the access log via `logger_name access`, with a configurable log level defaulting to DEBUG.

Make upgraded streams work through `encode`, `intercept` with `handle_response`, and access logging, so that nothing writes to the response after hijack, a 101 is the final response for an upgrade, and the proxy copies bytes on the raw connection rather than through the recording response writer.
Keep HTTP/2 extended CONNECT (RFC 8441) upgrades working, and HTTP/1.1 upgrades working in detached mode.
Add `reverse_proxy` stream metrics: active streams, streams closed by result, stream duration, and bytes to and from the backend, with each stream accounted exactly once.
Document the new options (`stream_detached`, `stream_logs`, `skip_handshake`, log level) in the config surface for both Caddyfile and JSON.

Add integration tests in `caddytest/integration` using a real server and real clients covering: streams surviving and being closed across reloads in each mode, extended CONNECT over h2, upgrades through `encode` and `intercept`, and detached streams with access logging.
Add unit tests for each piece of code changed.

constraints: The default behaviour (upgraded streams closed on reload, existing close-delay honoured) must stay unchanged.
Existing test suites must stay green.
stream_detached is opt-in; stream handshake logging default is logged; stream close log level default is DEBUG.
